title: Agentlet-based playbook runner for ad-hoc support workflows
creator: Aisha Khatri
description:
Problem: On-call engineers and support teams frequently run ad-hoc, multi-step remediation sequences that are only lightly documented in runbooks. Those workflows are error-prone, hard to audit, and difficult to safely automate across Dedicated and Private deployments.

Goal: Build an 'agentlet' playbook runner — a lightweight, auditable runtime that converts runbook steps into idempotent task primitives and executes them as transactional tasks with built-in pause/resume, manual approval gates, and automatic rollback where possible. The runner should integrate with existing runbooks-as-tasks concepts, tie into audit logs/KMS, and be usable both from Console and via a CLI for on-call flows.

Scope:
- Define a small set of task primitives (api_call, kubectl, sql_query, wait_for_metric, notify) and a JSON/YAML playbook schema.
- Implement a managed agentlet service in ops namespace that fetches playbooks, executes tasks with retries/backoff, and streams events to Console.
- Add permission boundaries: RBAC checks, KMS-based secrets retrieval, scoped service accounts for Private deployments.
- Wire audit events to syslog / Cloud Audit and add a Console timeline view.
- Provide a minimal CLI that wraps playbook invocation with approval flows for interactive remediation.

Non-goals: full long-running workflow engine, complex branching DSL, replacing full orchestrators (Argo, Airflow).
updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Platform, and SecOps. Agreed to start with 6 core primitives and YAML-first schema. Action: eng to prototype runner API and a demo playbook for 'KV cache warm restart'.

2026-02-20: Prototype PoC completed. PoC executed a two-step playbook (drain node -> restart inference worker) in staging. Observed edge-case where node drain API can return 202 and later fail — added explicit wait_for_metric primitive. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/opstools/pull/214

2026-02-25: Security review kickoff. SecOps requested KMS envelope pattern for inline secrets and a configurable allowlist for kubectl verbs. We scoped out plan to encrypt secret blobs and restrict kubectl to read/list for no-privilege playbooks. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/Agentlet+Design

2026-03-01: Design review with Console team. Decided to expose playbook audit timeline and a 'dry-run' simulation mode in Console. UX will show per-step logs and a link-to-PR for the runbook source. Early mock: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1a2b-agentlet-mock

2026-03-03: Implementation started. Marco landed initial runner that schedules tasks, persists step state to opsdb, and emits events to kafka. Open issues: EXP-12 (idempotency key scheme), EXP-15 (retry semantics for sql_query), and EXP-18 (graceful shutdown of running playbooks). GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/opstools/compare/agentlet-runner
2026-03-05: Integration smoke test passed for staging Dedicated cluster. Next: add approval-gate webhook and implement RBAC policy enforcement. Estimated 2 sprints to beta release.
notes: Trade-offs considered: building atop Argo was evaluated but rejected due to heavyweight operator lifecycle and harder audit model across Private deployments. Lightweight agentlet is easier to ship and secure.
Open decision: how to model branching — currently we will support linear + conditional on metric thresholds; full DAGs deferred.
Follow-ups: add playbook templating with parameter substitution, implement team-level allowlists, and add SLO-aware safety checks (e.g., avoid mass restarts under high traffic).
